audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer names "Majestic Roar" twice (wants.you[2], wants.foe[1]). Volibear has no such ability.
audit.why: Majestic Roar was pre-rework Volibear’s fear. The current kit is The Relentless Storm (P), Thundering Smash (Q), Frenzied Maul (W), Sky Splitter (E), Stormbringer (R). A player looking for "Majestic Roar" finds nothing on his bar.
audit.corrected: The tool that actually breaks a Flamespitter kite is Sky Splitter (E), a 1200-range bolt that slows and shields him only if he stands in his own blast. The approach tool is Thundering Smash (Q).

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere states that Thundering Smash grants ghosting.
audit.why: Ghosting means Volibear walks through the minion wave for the full 4s. Rumble’s standard kite — back off and put casters between you — simply does not work here, and that is the single most useful thing to know about his approach.
audit.corrected: Thundering Smash makes him ghosted with bonus move speed for 4s (doubled while facing you); the stun lands on his next basic attack, which is also an auto-reset. Kite it with Electro Harpoon, not with minions.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three places claim Volibear deals percent-max-health damage — wants.foe[2] "percent-max-HP Stormbringer R bite", late "percent-max-HP damage on Stormbringer bite", whys[6] "percent-max-HP bites".
audit.why: No ability in Volibear’s kit deals percent-max-health damage. Stormbringer is a leap dealing flat damage with bonus-AD and AP ratios — it is not a bite at all. Frenzied Maul is the bite, and its bonus damage scales off Volibear’s own bonus health (6%), not the target’s max health.
audit.corrected: The real scaling story is Frenzied Maul: every point of health Volibear buys raises its damage, so his tank items make him tankier and hit harder simultaneously. That is why 2-item Volibear outpaces Rumble.

audit.whatIsWrong: late says "Never let him Thundering Smash onto your backline".
audit.why: Thundering Smash is a 300-range self-buff approach, not a backline entry tool. Stormbringer is the 550-range leap that actually lands him on a backline.
audit.corrected: Name Stormbringer as the dive, and place the Equalizer carpet on his landing zone rather than trying to intercept a Q.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns says "Track it before every engage" without a single number.
audit.why: Thundering Smash is 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s. At rank 1 that is a 12-second window after he uses it — long enough to run two full Flamespitter rotations (Q is 10s at rank 1). Without the number the advice is unactionable.
audit.corrected: Stated the 12s rank-1 cooldown and the 4s ghosted window explicitly.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0] and whys[0] both treat Frenzied Maul as level-1 burst.
audit.why: Frenzied Maul’s second-cast bonus damage is 6% of Volibear’s bonus health. At level 1 with no items his bonus health is near zero, so the ability is a heal and an on-hit application, not a burst spike. Telling a Rumble to fear level-1 W burst makes him play the lane backwards.
audit.corrected: At level 1 W is sustain, not damage; it becomes a damage spike only once he has bought health.

audit.whatIsWrong: No mention that Sky Splitter only shields Volibear when he is inside his own blast.
audit.why: It is a free read on his intent. Sky Splitter thrown at max range to poke gives him no shield; Sky Splitter dropped on his own feet means he is committing to a fight.
audit.corrected: Left as an audit note — no writable field had room for it without cutting something better.

audit.whatIsWrong: diff is "FAVOURED" with diffRating "4/10" while the matchup win rate is exactly 50.00% over 510 games, and the two layers disagree with each other.
audit.why: The content win array reads Volibear/Skill/Skill/Rumble/Skill/Rumble/Volibear (2-3-2, an even lane) but the full layer gives Rumble 5 of 7 stages. Both cannot be right, and 50.00% supports the content array.
audit.corrected: diff should be "EVEN" with diffRating "6/10", and full phases[0] and phases[6] should read "Volibear" with phases[2] and phases[4] "Skill" to match the content chart. NOT proposed as edits: "EVEN" is 4 chars against "FAVOURED" at 8, and the side labels differ in length, so every one of them falls outside the +/-10% band and would be rejected. Needs a hand fix.

edits.after: Double-cast Electro-Harpoon when Thundering Smash is down — both stacks double the slow and the MR shred

edits.after: Ghost through minions with Thundering Smash before your Q can out-damage his W bite-heal

edits.after: Two-plus items Volibear — every point of health he buys feeds Frenzied Maul — outraces your frontloaded damage; play for Equalizer placement rather than solo kills.

edits.before: Volibear's W bite into level-1 skirmish hurts before you have Danger Zone empowerment — respect his raw stat lead and Q from max range.
edits.after: Volibear's W heals more than it hurts at level 1 — its bonus damage scales off bonus health he has not bought. Respect stats, Q from max range.

edits.before: Late game Volibear's scaling hurts — his percent-max-HP damage on Stormbringer bite, bulk, and tank itemization mean your Flamespitter damage per trade falls off relative to what he can absorb. You are not trying to 1v1 him here; your job is Equalizer placement in teamfights, cutting his engages off at the threshold and slowing his team enough that your carries punish the dive. If you built Shadowflame into Zhonya's, you can bait his R dive, pop Zhonya's through the worst of it, and your team cleans up. Never let him Thundering Smash onto your backline without a preemptive Equalizer wall to soften the approach.
edits.after: Late game Volibear's scaling hurts — Frenzied Maul rises with every point of health he buys, so his tank items make him tankier and harder-hitting at once, and your Flamespitter damage per trade falls off relative to what he can absorb. You are not trying to 1v1 him here; your job is Equalizer placement in teamfights, cutting his engages off at the threshold and slowing his team enough that your carries punish the dive. If you built Shadowflame into Zhonya's, you can bait his R dive, pop Zhonya's through the worst of it, and your team cleans up. Never let him Stormbringer onto your backline without a preemptive Equalizer carpet on the landing zone.

edits.before: Heat management is the kit: ride 50-100, never overheat by accident. Only take the trade when Volibear's Thundering Smash is down.
edits.after: Heat management is the kit: ride 50-100, never overheat by accident. Trade only when Thundering Smash is down — a 12s window at rank 1.

edits.before: The Equalizer cuts lanes and teamfights in half — aim it across the path, not on heads. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Volibear's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: The Equalizer cuts lanes and teamfights in half — aim it across the path, not on heads. At 6 Stormbringer disables your tower, so being low under turret is not safe.

edits.after: - Volibear Thundering Smash (12s at rank 1): his engage and his auto-reset stun — kite the 4s ghosted window with E, then run the full pattern on its cooldown. - Your ultimate: kill windows only, never chip.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Frenzied Maul heals him every 5s — long trades just refill him.

notes: Volibear kit flags in champ-data/_kits/rumble.json are wrong for Rumble W: Scrap Shield carries derived flags "knockup" and "terrain". Verified on the wiki that Scrap Shield neither displaces nor creates terrain — those are derivation artifacts from the words "pulls up a shield". _missing-interactions.json repeats the error (knockup-enabler rows citing Scrap Shield as displacement). Do not let any writer build advice on them. Separately: The Equalizer is NOT a blockable projectile and does NOT create movement-blocking terrain (4.5s fire field, 35% slow) — the kit’s "terrain: creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes" flag on R is also a false positive, so wording like "wall off his escape" is misleading across many Rumble entries.
